bottom_line: In the CHARM-Overall programme, candesartan vs placebo reduced all-cause mortality with a covariate adjusted hazard ratio of 0.90 (95% CI 0.82–0.99).
implications: These results support that, in this programme, candesartan compared with placebo was associated with lower cardiovascular deaths (691 [18%] vs 769 [20%]) and lower cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (1150 [30.2%] vs 1310 [34.5%]) with adjusted hazard ratios below 1, while the all-cause mortality reduction was borderline by unadjusted analysis (p=0.055) but statistically significant after covariate adjustment (0.90 [0.82–0.99], p=0.032). The document also reports more discontinuations with candesartan due to renal function concerns, hypotension, and hyperkalaemia, so the findings do not establish benefit without these tolerability trade-offs.

major_points.text: Three parallel, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials in distinct heart-failure populations were integrated in the overall programme.
major_points.quote:
three parallel, independent, integrated, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled,
                                                                          clinical trials comparing candesartan with placebo in three
                                                                          distinct but complementary populations of patients with
                                                                          symptomatic heart failure.

major_points.text: Overall, 7601 patients were randomly assigned to candesartan titrated to 32 mg once daily or matching placebo and followed for at least 2 years.
major_points.quote:
Overall, 7601 patients (7599 with data) were
      randomly assigned candesartan (n=3803, titrated to 32 mg
      once daily) or matching placebo (n=3796), and followed up
      for at least 2 years.

major_points.text: The primary outcome of the overall programme was all-cause death.
major_points.quote:
The primary outcome of the overall programme was all-
     cause death.

major_points.text: All-cause mortality was 886 (23%) with candesartan vs 945 (25%) with placebo; covariate adjusted HR 0.90 (0.82–0.99), p=0.032.
major_points.quote:
886 (23%) in the candesartan group and 945 (25%) in
      the placebo group died from any cause (unadjusted
      hazard ratio 0·91 [95% CI 0·83–1·00)], p=0·055;
      covariate adjusted 0·90 [0·82–0·99], p=0·032

major_points.text: Cardiovascular death or hospital admission for CHF (primary outcome for component trials) occurred in 1150 (30.2%) vs 1310 (34.5%); adjusted hazard ratio 0.82 (0.75–0.88), p<0.0001.

subgroups.text: Prespecified subgroup analyses were done using tests for heterogeneity to assess interactions between treatment and baseline variables.
subgroups.quote:
Prespecified subgroup analyses were done, each using a
      test for heterogeneity to assess for possible interactions

subgroups.text: No significant heterogeneity across the three trials for all-cause mortality impact (interaction test p=0.37).
subgroups.quote:
There was, however, no significant
      heterogeneity across the three trials in the impact of
      candesartan on all-cause mortality (figure 3) or cardio-
      vascular deaths or hospital admission for CHF (interaction
      test, p=0·37 and p=0·43, respectively).

subgroups.text: Reductions in death were seen among patients with LVEF of 40% or less, with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (0.88 [0.79–0.98], p=0.018).
subgroups.quote:
The reductions in death, particularly cardiovascular
      death, were seen among patients with LVEF of 40% or less,
      with significant reductions in all-cause mortality (0·88
      [0·79–0·98], p=0·018)

subgroups.text: The reduction in risk of cardiovascular death or hospital admission for heart failure with candesartan was similar in men and women.
subgroups.quote:
The reduction in risk of cardiovascular death or hospital
     admission for heart failure with candesartan was similar in
     men and women (figure 5).

subgroups.text: Patients aged 75 years or older showed as great a benefit with candesartan as younger patients.
subgroups.quote:
the 1736 patients
      aged 75 years or older showed as great a benefit with
      candesartan as did younger patients.

subgroups.text: Similar effectiveness was noted in patients with LVEF higher or lower than 40%.
subgroups.quote:
Particularly
      noteworthy was the similar effectiveness of candesartan in
      patients with LVEF higher or lower than 40% (figure 5).

harms.text: Discontinuation for hypotension was 132 (3.5%) with candesartan vs 66 (1.7%) with placebo (p<0.0001).
Discontinuation for increase in serum creatinine was 234 (6.2%) vs 115 (3.0) (p<0.0001).
Potassium concentration of 6.0 mmol/L or higher occurred in 31 (2%) vs 15 (1%) (p=0.017).
harms.quote:
A

      or higher was seen in 31 (2%) of 1294
      candesartan and 15 (1%) of 1310

inclusion_criteria.quote:

     treated with an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor

     with an angiotensin-converting-enzyme inhibitor because of
     previous intolerance (CHARM-Alternative).

analysis_methods.text: Analysis was by intention to treat.
analysis_methods.quote: Analysis was by intention to treat.

analysis_methods.text: Programme had more than 85% power to detect around a 14% reduction in mortality at significance level 0.05 (logrank test), assuming 8% annual placebo mortality.
analysis_methods.quote:
We estimated an annual overall
      mortality in the placebo group of 8% and, on that basis,
      the programme of investigation had more than 85%
      power to detect around a 14% reduction in mortality at a
      significance level of 0·05, based on the logrank test.

analysis_methods.text: Time-to-event analyses used the logrank test and Kaplan-Meier plots; hazard ratios estimated with stratified logrank test.
analysis_methods.quote:
All time-to-event variables were analysed with
                        the logrank test and displayed on Kaplan-Meier plots
      according to treatment. We estimated the hazard ratios
      and 95% CI comparing treatments, stratified by trial, with
      a stratified logrank test.

analysis_methods.text: Covariate-adjusted Cox regression model fitted with prespecified baseline covariates to adjust hazard ratio.
analysis_methods.quote:
a covariate-adjusted
      Cox’s regression model was fitted with the prespecified
      baseline covariates shown in table 1 to adjust the hazard
      ratio for other factors that might affect prognosis.
